description: PrUn community-derived ship BLUEPRINT construction data: component volumes, component mass observations, structural element and build-time formulas. Complements shippingBlueprint.ts (which covers the blueprint Performance panel, not construction). Values transcribed verbatim; unknowns from the source ('?') are null.

structuralElements.note: Number of SSC materials needed for the ship.

componentVolumesM3.note: Component volume is consistent regardless of other blueprint choices.

ftlTanks.note: Exact — an STL ship can be built without an FTL tank (no tank contributes no volume).

stlTanks.note: Relative volumes exact, absolute anchor unclear (no ship exists without a tank); Small = 70 m3 chosen because it produces round numbers.

ftlEngines.note: Exact, relative to the no-drive scenario.

stlEngines.note: Relative volumes — the STL drive cannot be removed. Optimized to account for all remaining ship volume (the made-up remainder could instead be split between the small STL tank and the Standard engine).

componentMass.note: Mass of components is NOT consistent — it changes with other design choices. Larger cargo bays sometimes make tanks add more mass, sometimes less.

cargoBayMassByTankLoadout.note: Mass added per cargo bay, by fuel-tank loadout.

tankMassByCargoBay.note: Mass added by a tank depending on the installed cargo bay. Uncertain source values ('251?', '52?') kept with certain: false.

componentSizeEffect.note: Do individual component sizes adjust ship mass/volume when installed? Evidence points to no — component mass/vol is irrelevant to ship size.

ftlFieldEmitters.note: Source-code numbers; no known way to apply them correctly. Dev blog (2020-07-20 warp-drive-time-244) says emitters must together span at least the ship's total volume, but requirements neither add up to the span numbers nor match sphere radii/diameters.
